strings: Gann's Reclamation is a Horde quest offered by the wandering tauren exile Gann Stonespire in the southern Barrens. Deeply aggrieved by the dwarven archaeological dig at Bael Modan that displaced his tribe, Gann enlists travelers to strike back by slaying the site's workers and retrieving their leader's journal.

Before the Prospector's cannons and pickaxes broke the earth, the red bluffs south of the Barrens were the ancestral birthplace and hunting grounds of Gann Stonespire's clan. When the dwarves arrived from Ironforge to establish Bael Modan, the tauren were violently pushed out or killed to make room for massive quarries and trenches. With peaceful protests ignored and diplomacy exhausted, Gann now walks the dust of the southern road in solitude, plotting a bloody restitution for his fallen kin.

The dwarven operation at Bael Modan spares little thought for the land or its stewards. Ripping open hillsides with steam engines and heavy explosives, the expedition under Prospector Khazgorm tore deep into the earth. Gann's task is simple and uncompromising: thin the ranks of the Bael'dun excavators and foremen tearing up the sacred soil, slay Khazgorm himself, and seize the prospector's personal excavation notes to discover what the Alliance invaders are truly after.

Gann Stonespire is a solitary tauren survivor whose tribe once lived in the southern Barrens. After dwarven excavators displaced his people and killed those who resisted, Gann took to pacing the southern highway, seeking justice and revenge against the encroaching Alliance dig site.

Bael Modan represents a fortified Alliance stronghold deep inside Kalimdor territory, making the defense of Gann's claim both an act of honor and strategic containment.
For the Shu'halo, Gann's plight is an infuriating reminder of how little the Alliance respects the Earth Mother, using dynamite and iron gears to tear apart ancestral burial grounds.

Bael Modan sits directly atop the ancestral lands of Gann's tribe. When the dwarves arrived, their relentless digging, loud machinery, and blasting drove the tauren from their home and cost many innocent lives. Having exhausted all peaceful overtures, Gann seeks retribution and aims to reclaim his people's sacred homeland by force.

Plainstrider Menace is an introductory hunting task assigned by Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. Newly arrived Horde adventurers are directed to cull the native plainstriders scavenging the settlement's supply routes, serving both as pest control and as an initial test of hunting prowess.

The Crossroads sits at the logistical heart of Kalimdor, coordinating supply caravans across the harsh savanna. However, the arid terrain leaves local wildlife desperate for sustenance. Flocks of tall, flightless plainstriders roaming just east of the outpost have taken to picking at food crates and disrupting the settlement's lifeline. To protect these vulnerable provisions, the shaman Sergra Darkthorn dispatches travelers to cull the aggressive birds before they inflict serious damage on the outpost's stores.

While pest management is an immediate practical goal, Sergra views the plainstriders as a measuring stick for newcomers. She considers the birds simple prey—easy game intended to teach young hunters how to survive the elements and track quarry in the sun-baked plains. Bringing back their sharp beaks proves that a hunter has the patience and basic martial skill required to face the fiercer beasts native to the Barrens.

Flocks of plainstriders east of the Crossroads have grown bold enough to raid food supplies and harass passing supply lines. Sergra Darkthorn orders them culled to preserve the settlement's vital provisions.

The Zhevra is an early hunting trial issued by Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. As part of a progressing test of martial prowess across the savannas of the Barrens, young hunters are charged with tracking down swift zhevra runners and taking their powerful hooves.
A Step Up in the Savanna

Following an initial cull of the Barrens' overgrown plainstriders, Sergra Darkthorn directs fledgling Horde warriors toward slightly more formidable game. The striped zhevras roam in herds across the northern and southern plains. While not the apex predators of the savanna, they are fleet-footed herd beasts known for their stubborn endurance and powerful, bone-cracking kicks.

To Sergra, this hunt is less about securing trade goods and more about testing an adventurer's developing edge. She demands four intact hooves as physical proof of the kill, warning that the beast's rear kick has enough force to drop a grown tauren onto its haunches. Proving oneself against these fleet runners earns a hunter entry into even deadlier trials against the predatory prowlers of the plains.
Sergra Darkthorn, an experienced orc shaman stationed at the Crossroads in the central Barrens, issues this trial to test growing Horde warriors.

Revenge of Gann is a Horde quest in the southern Barrens where the grieving tauren exile Gann Stonespire plans retribution against the Bael Modan expedition. Having eliminated Prospector Khazgorm, Gann directs travelers into the dwarven fortress to gather volatile munitions for an explosive counterattack.
A Taste of Their Own Medicine

Prospector Khazgorm's death delivered a setback to the Bael Modan dig site, but Gann Stonespire knows it is merely temporary. Dwarven operations rarely pause for long, and a new foreman will soon arrive to oversee the machines gutting his ancestral territory. Refusing to watch the earth suffer further excavation, Gann resolves to strike back using the invaders' own technology. By turning their demolitions gear into an instrument of sabotage, he plans to rupture their stronghold from within.

Bael Modan's fortress serves as both an excavation base and a fortified garrison, outfitted with soldiers, riflemen, and officers protecting dwarven interests in the Barrens. Gann discovers that the defenders stockpile materials suited for industrial demolition: nitroglycerin, wood pulp, and sodium nitrate. He tasks Horde allies with infiltrating the perimeter to strip these volatile components directly from dwarven ranks, stockpiling enough raw material to assemble a devastating satchel charge.
Why is Gann Stonespire seeking revenge?

The Ironforge dwarves of Bael Modan overran Gann's ancestral homeland, desecrating the soil and driving his people out to establish their excavation site. After slaying the chief prospector and recovering his journal, Gann aims to halt their ongoing destruction permanently.

For the tauren, Bael Modan represents a grievous wound against the Earth Mother, making the sabotage of dwarven machinery a spiritual and territorial duty.

Apothecary Helbrim of the Royal Apothecary Society tasks Horde adventurers with gathering fungal spores around the oases of the Barrens. The strange, mutative energies coursing through these springs have altered the local flora into potent reagents. Helbrim seeks to harvest these unique specimens to brew concoctions for his colleague in Thunder Bluff.

The Barrens is generally an arid, sun-scorched savanna, yet its oases—such as the Forgotten Pools, the Lushwater Oasis, and the Stagnant Oasis—burst with unnatural vitality. A curious surge of life energy flows from these waters, warping and invigorating the plants and beasts that drink from them. Laden mushrooms growing along the muddy banks absorb these intense currents, filling their spores with rare properties that pique the curiosity of passing alchemists.
The Royal Apothecary Society in Kalimdor

Though stationed far from the Undercity at the Crossroads, Apothecary Helbrim remains devoted to the research of the Royal Apothecary Society. Recognizing the strange potency of Kalimdor's native reagents, he collects these altered spores to craft powerful mixtures. The specimens gathered here are destined for Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff, demonstrating the subtle, far-reaching scientific efforts the Forsaken carry out across allied lands.

Revenge of Gann marks the final strike in Gann Stonespire's vendetta against the dwarves of Bael Modan. Armed with a tailored explosive charge crafted from stolen dwarven plans, an agent of the Horde is tasked with detonating the expedition's prized flying machine to avenge the fallen Stonespire tribe.

The Bael Modan excavation is more than an intrusive mining operation; it is an armed fortress planted directly atop the ancestral grounds of the displaced Stonespire tauren. Key to the Prospectors' operational reach and military prowess is their gyrocopter flying machine. Stationed on a watchtower above the dig, the mechanical aircraft surveys the surrounding Barrens, protects supply lines, and acts as a hovering symbol of the Alliance's brazen intrusion into kalimdorian soil.

Having recovered the plans of Prospector Khazgorm, Gann Stonespire crafts a specialized explosive charge dubbed the Explosive Stick of Gann. By planting this volatile munition upon the flying machine, Gann ensures the dwarves' technological hubris becomes their undoing. The resulting explosion shatters a vital military asset, dealing a humiliating blow to the Bael'dun contingent and honoring the spirits of the lost tribe.
Why does Gann want to destroy the flying machine specifically?

The flying machine is both a weapon of war and a crucial part of Bael Modan's infrastructure, granting the dwarves aerial reconnaissance. More importantly to Gann, it represents a blatant icon of dwarven power and an insulting presence towering over the land his slaughtered tribe once called home.

Lost Necklace is an introductory task in southern Elwynn Forest given by "Auntie" Bernice Stonefield. Suspecting theft by the rival clan's mischievous young boy, Bernice sends adventurers across the road to confront Billy Maclure and retrieve her missing heirloom.

The Stonefield and Maclure families share adjoining land in southern Elwynn Forest, but very little goodwill passes between them. When "Auntie" Bernice Stonefield discovers her cherished necklace is missing, she wastes no time pointing the finger at the youngest of the rival household. Convinced that young Billy Maclure snuck onto her farm and snatched the jewelry, the bitter widow asks any willing traveler to cross over to the vineyards, track down the boy, and demand its return.

Confronting Billy Maclure at the neighboring vineyard quickly complicates the matter. Billy indignantly denies taking the necklace, claiming he is no thief. However, with a knowing grin, he hints that he might just know what actually became of the trinket—provided someone satisfies his rumbling stomach with a fresh pork pie first.

Kolkar Leaders begins a campaign led by the orc Regthar Deathgate to crush rising centaur warlords in the Barrens. The nomadic Kolkar have plagued the tauren for generations, but newly emerged chieftains are organizing their disorganized bands into a genuine military threat. Regthar tasks champions of the Horde with cutting down Barak Kodobane at the Forgotten Pools before his influence can spread.
A Rising Menace in the Drylands

For countless years, the horse-bodied centaur have terrorized Kalimdor, driving the nomadic tauren nearly to extinction before Thrall's Horde arrived to turn the tide. In the Barrens, the dominant Kolkar tribe generally roams in scattered, fractured marauding parties. Recently, however, aggressive chieftains have begun uniting the disparate bands, turning simple raiding parties into a cohesive military threat capable of contesting the Horde's fortified outposts.

Stationed in an encampment west of the Crossroads, the orc warrior Regthar Deathgate recognized that the Kolkar rely heavily on sheer bravado and brute force to maintain cohesion. Without strong commanders, their raiders degenerate into infighting. To blunt their advance, Regthar directs Horde adventurers to cut off the head of the snake, starting with Barak Kodobane, an ambitious leader camping near the verdant waters of the Forgotten Pools.

Slaying Barak Kodobane deals a significant blow to the northern Kolkar encampments, yet Regthar knows Barak is merely the vanguard of a broader movement. His elimination marks the opening salvo of a concerted campaign to dismantle the Kolkar high command, paving the way to hunt down fellow chieftains Verog the Dervish and Hezrul Bloodmark across the Barrens.

Barak Kodobane is a fierce Kolkar centaur leader who rallied marauders around the Forgotten Pools north of the Crossroads. Known for his wit and cruelty, he proved far more dangerous than ordinary nomadic raiders by organizing disparate clans into an offensive threat against the Horde.
